label: Target types
description: What a weapon can hit (on a weapon) or what kind of target a unit is (from its mobility; a tiny or small ground unit counts as infantry). Fliers are in one of two air layers: low air, which most direct-fire weapons can reach, and high air, which only anti-air weapons reach.

terms.label: Infantry
terms.description: Soldiers, animals and other infantry-sized ground targets, including small ground drones.

terms.label: Low air
terms.description: Helicopters, flying drones, jetpack troops and other low fliers. Most direct-fire weapons can reach them, not only anti-air.

terms.label: High air
terms.description: Jets and airships flying high above the fight. Only anti-air weapons reach them.
terms.source_rule: On a weapon: in a commanded game, list it for any weapon the sources say can attack air units, unless the game splits its fliers and this weapon cannot reach its jets or airships. In a piloted game (control piloted or both in data/games.json), list it only for a weapon built to bring down aircraft: the sources call it anti-air or anti-aircraft, it locks onto jets, or it is a flak gun. A weapon that could hit a passing jet by chance does not count.

terms.label: Naval
terms.description: Ships, boats and submarines. Research only.
terms.source_rule: On a weapon: in a game with ships or boats, list naval on every weapon that lists ground-vehicle, unless the sources say it cannot reach ships. In a game without ships or boats, never list it.
